title: Lighting, PPFD, DLI, Photoperiod & Canopy Uniformity
level: Environmental, Irrigation & Fertigation Systems Specialist / advanced specialization development
intendedAudience: Cultivation personnel responsible for canopy-light measurement, mapping, fixture verification and evidence-based lighting handoff
prerequisites: Plant-Environment Measurement & Crop Response or equivalent measurement foundation
evidencePolicy: Lighting instruction uses controlled university-extension measurement guidance plus governed cannabis/environment material. PPFD, DLI, photoperiod and spectrum relationships are taught as measurement/response concepts; non-cannabis crop values and study-specific cannabis treatments are not universal facility targets.
assessmentPolicy: Development-only until technical/assessment review, accessibility review and pilot evidence are complete. Course completion does not authorize electrical work, fixture modification, photoperiod changes or production setpoint changes outside assigned authority.
description: Develops specialist measurement and interpretation of canopy light through PPFD mapping, DLI, photoperiod, spectrum, fixture geometry, uniformity, crop architecture and cross-system environmental context.
learningOutcomes: Design and execute a repeatable canopy PPFD mapping plan with controlled measurement height, orientation, grid geometry and meter verification.
Calculate and interpret DLI from representative PPFD and photoperiod while explaining why equal DLI can arise from different intensity-duration combinations.
Evaluate canopy-light uniformity using distribution, range and spatial pattern rather than relying on a single average or center measurement.
Interpret photoperiod, spectrum, fixture geometry and canopy architecture as interacting lighting variables without overstating universal crop-response claims.
Produce a lighting verification report that links measurement quality, canopy distribution, operating state, crop/environment context and authorized next action.
